title: Overload protection observability plan (metrics + alerts) — draft
body:
Owner: Aisha (SRE)
Last reviewed with: Logan (Telemetry), Allison (Obs standards), Ethan (Gateway), Mina (Routing), Sofia (Runtime)

Purpose
- Define the first-pass metrics + alerting strategy for Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding.
- Keep metric cardinality bounded and queries cheap.
- Ensure we can answer quickly during incidents:
  1) Are we shedding / rejecting?
  2) Where in the stack is it happening (gateway vs routing vs runtime)?
  3) Is it protecting latency/error rates (or causing false positives)?
  4) Which regions/models/tiers are impacted?

Non-goals (for this doc)
- Full dashboard spec (see Confluence dashboard page).
- Full tracing and log schema. (We’ll add a short section on how to tie metrics to traces via correlation IDs.)

Principles / naming conventions
1) Metric names
- Prefix: redwood_overload_* for all overload protection metrics.
- Component prefix in label rather than name unless it clarifies type (gateway/routing/runtime).
- Use units in metric name where not obvious:
  - *_seconds (histograms)
  - *_total (counters)
  - *_ratio (gauges 0..1)

2) Label/Dimension policy (cardinality)
Allowed labels (generally OK)
- region: e.g., us-east, us-west, eu-central
- environment: prod|staging
- tier: hosted_free|hosted_pro|hosted_enterprise|dedicated (if it runs through same gateway)
- route: chat_completions|completions|embeddings|rerank (small, fixed set)
- model_family: e.g., llama3|qwen2|mistral (NOT full model version string if it explodes)
- breaker_name: small controlled set (see below)
- reason: small controlled enum (see below)

Avoid labels (do not ship to Prometheus)
- tenant_id / org_id / api_key_id
- request_id / correlation_id
- model_version with many variants (e.g., llama3-70b-instruct-2025-11-18)
- user_agent, sdk_version (use logs/analytics pipeline instead)
- prompt_length_bucket by fine-grained bucket (keep buckets coarse)
- error_message strings

If we need per-tenant debugging
- Use logs with sampled structured events + correlation_id.
- Optional: emit high-cardinality dimensions only to our telemetry warehouse (not Prometheus) via the “metrics-to-events” stream. (Logan to confirm pipeline contract.)

3) Histogram guidance
- Prefer histograms for latency and queue wait, but keep bucket counts sane.
- For GPU/runtime metrics, prefer gauges for instantaneous saturation + a small number of histograms for queue wait.

4) Error taxonomy alignment
- Reasons/codes should map to ADR-014 stable overload error codes.
- We should be able to compute “overload errors vs true 5xx” from metrics, and SLO-toolkit should classify accordingly (see slo-toolkit PR-132).


Metric inventory (proposed)

A) Gateway admission control + breaker framework
1) Requests evaluated / admitted / rejected
- redwood_overload_admission_evaluations_total (counter)
  labels: region, environment, tier, route
- redwood_overload_admission_admitted_total (counter)
  labels: region, environment, tier, route
- redwood_overload_admission_rejected_total (counter)
  labels: region, environment, tier, route, reason, breaker_name, http_status

Reason enum (draft — keep small)
- concurrency_cap
- token_bucket_empty
- breaker_open
- dependency_unhealthy
- regional_capacity_low
- runtime_saturated
- request_too_large (if we use degradation: max_tokens cap / prompt cap)

Breaker name enum (draft; controlled by policy engine)
- gateway_global
- gateway_by_route
- gateway_by_model_family
- routing_fallback_guard
- runtime_admission

2) Breaker state
- redwood_overload_breaker_state (gauge)
  0=closed, 1=half_open, 2=open
  labels: region, environment, breaker_name, tier, route, model_family
  Notes: keep route/model_family only where we have a small fixed set; otherwise omit.

- redwood_overload_breaker_transitions_total (counter)
  labels: region, environment, breaker_name, from_state, to_state, reason

3) Retry-After correctness (contract)
Goal: ensure clients don’t cause retry storms and we meet “stable semantics”.
- redwood_overload_retry_after_missing_total (counter)
  labels: region, environment, route, http_status, reason
- redwood_overload_retry_after_seconds (histogram)
  labels: region, environment, route
  Notes: record the header value we send for 429/503 overload responses.

4) Policy evaluation
- redwood_overload_policy_eval_total (counter)
  labels: region, environment, outcome (allow|deny|degrade|fallback)
- redwood_overload_policy_eval_latency_seconds (histogram)
  labels: region, environment

B) Smart Routing (fallback / loop prevention)
1) Fallback attempts and outcomes
- redwood_overload_fallback_attempts_total (counter)
  labels: region, environment, route, model_family, target (model_variant|region), outcome (success|failed|skipped)
  Notes: “target” must be coarse (e.g., region or “compat_variant”). Don’t use full model name.

- redwood_overload_fallback_blocked_total (counter)
  labels: region, environment, route, reason (loop_prevention|max_retries|policy_disallow)

2) Routing queue / backlog (if present in routing layer)
- redwood_overload_routing_backlog_depth (gauge)
  labels: region, environment

C) Serving runtime saturation signals
(See runtime notes; keep to a small set that we trust + can interpret)

1) Queue depths
- redwood_runtime_prefill_queue_depth (gauge)
  labels: region, environment, pool (shared|dedicated if shared metric), model_family
- redwood_runtime_decode_queue_depth (gauge)
  labels: region, environment, pool, model_family

2) Queue wait time
- redwood_runtime_queue_wait_seconds (histogram)
  labels: region, environment, stage (prefill|decode), model_family

3) Token throughput saturation proxy
- redwood_runtime_tokens_per_second (gauge)
  labels: region, environment, model_family
- redwood_runtime_tokens_per_second_capacity (gauge)
  labels: region, environment, model_family
- redwood_overload_runtime_saturation_ratio (gauge)
  labels: region, environment, model_family
  definition: tokens_per_second / capacity (clamped 0..1.5)

4) Memory pressure proxy
- redwood_runtime_kv_cache_utilization_ratio (gauge)
  labels: region, environment, model_family
- redwood_runtime_memory_fragmentation_ratio (gauge) (optional; only if runtime team is confident)
  labels: region, environment

D) Customer-visible overload errors (from gateway)
We need a metric that matches what customers observe.
- redwood_api_overload_responses_total (counter)
  labels: region, environment, route, http_status (429|503), error_code
  Where error_code is the stable code from ADR-014 (e.g., OVERLOAD_GATEWAY, OVERLOAD_RUNTIME, OVERLOAD_DEPENDENCY, OVERLOAD_CAPACITY).

Also ensure we can compute overall response counts for rate calculations:
- redwood_api_requests_total (counter)
  labels: region, environment, route, http_status_class (2xx|4xx|5xx)


Alerting strategy (draft)

Severity model
- Page (SEV2/SEV1): high confidence user impact or imminent SLO burn; must be actionable.
- Ticket / Slack notify: early warning, tuning required, or low-confidence signals.
- No alerts on raw saturation gauges alone unless combined with impact.

Warmup / tuning plan
Phase 1 (dark launch / canary)
- All alerts in “notify-only” mode to #eng-oncall + #eng-sre, no paging.
- Daily false-positive review (15 min) with oncall + Aisha + component owner.
- Record thresholds + changes in tuning log (append-only section at bottom).

Phase 2 (regional canary)
- Promote 2–3 alerts to paging for the canary region only.
- Gate with a “requests > N/min” condition to avoid noise off-hours.

Phase 3 (GA)
- Paging alerts enabled all regions.
- Add multi-window burn-rate alerts for overload error SLI.

Recommended alerts (initial)

1) Overload response rate too high (customer visible)
Intent: Detect sustained shedding/rejections impacting customers.
Query (PromQL example):
- overload_rate = sum by (region, route) (rate(redwood_api_overload_responses_total{environment="prod"}[5m]))
- req_rate = sum by (region, route) (rate(redwood_api_requests_total{environment="prod"}[5m]))
- overload_ratio = overload_rate / clamp_min(req_rate, 1)

Alert (page) suggestion:
- if overload_ratio > 0.02 for 10m AND req_rate > 50
  labels to include in alert: region, route
  runbook: hosted-overload-circuit-breaker-runbook (Confluence)

2) Breaker flapping (bad tuning or unstable dependency)
Intent: Identify noisy breaker transitions (often creates customer confusion + hides root cause).
Query:
- sum by (region, breaker_name) (rate(redwood_overload_breaker_transitions_total{environment="prod"}[10m])) > 0.2
(> ~2 transitions / 10m)

Alert (ticket/notify) suggestion:
- notify when > 0.2 for 15m
- page when > 0.5 for 10m AND overload_ratio rising

3) Runtime saturation with impact (gate saturation by overload errors)
Intent: Avoid paging on saturation alone; page when saturation correlates with overload responses.
Queries:
- sat = avg by (region, model_family) (redwood_overload_runtime_saturation_ratio{environment="prod"})
- overload = sum by (region, model_family) (rate(redwood_api_overload_responses_total{environment="prod", error_code=~"OVERLOAD_RUNTIME.*"}[5m]))

Alert (page) suggestion:
- sat > 0.95 for 10m AND overload > 2/s for 5m

4) Retry-After missing on overload responses (contract regression)
Intent: Prevent retry storms; this is a correctness/SLO-protection feature.
Query:
- sum by (region, route) (rate(redwood_overload_retry_after_missing_total{environment="prod"}[15m]))

Alert (notify -> page once stable)
- notify if > 0 for 15m in any region/route (during canary)
- page if > 0.1/s for 10m (GA)

5) Dependency brownout causing overload (optional; depends on dependency health metric availability)
If we already have dependency health check metrics:
- redwood_dependency_health (gauge 0/1) or error rate per dependency.
We can correlate:
- overload responses with reason=dependency_unhealthy.

Query:
- sum by (region) (rate(redwood_overload_admission_rejected_total{reason="dependency_unhealthy", environment="prod"}[5m]))

Alert (page) suggestion:
- > 1/s for 10m AND dependency health failing (if available)

Multi-window burn rate alert (future, after SLO policy final)
Once SLO toolkit classification is finalized, use a standard burn-rate approach on “successful requests” where overload errors are either:
- included as errors (most customer experience views), and/or
- tracked separately as “overload exceptions” depending on the SLO doc.

Draft burn-rate PromQL sketch (not final):
- error_ratio_5m = (rate(redwood_api_overload_responses_total[5m]) + rate(redwood_api_requests_total{http_status_class="5xx"}[5m]))
  / clamp_min(rate(redwood_api_requests_total[5m]), 1)

(Need to align with Hosted API SLO policy doc before shipping.)


Example dashboard queries (PromQL snippets)

A) Shed/reject rate by reason (gateway)
sum by (region, reason) (rate(redwood_overload_admission_rejected_total{environment="prod"}[5m]))

B) Breaker state heatmap (open breakers)
max by (region, breaker_name) (redwood_overload_breaker_state{environment="prod"} == 2)

C) Overload ratio by route
(
  sum by (region, route) (rate(redwood_api_overload_responses_total{environment="prod"}[5m]))
)
/
clamp_min(
  sum by (region, route) (rate(redwood_api_requests_total{environment="prod"}[5m])),
  1
)

D) Runtime queue depth vs overload errors (two panels)
- Queue depth:
avg by (region, model_family) (redwood_runtime_decode_queue_depth{environment="prod"})
- Overload errors:
sum by (region, model_family) (rate(redwood_api_overload_responses_total{environment="prod", error_code=~"OVERLOAD_RUNTIME.*"}[5m]))

E) Fallback success rate
sum(rate(redwood_overload_fallback_attempts_total{outcome="success", environment="prod"}[5m]))
/
clamp_min(sum(rate(redwood_overload_fallback_attempts_total{environment="prod"}[5m])), 1)


Instrumentation notes / open questions
1) model_family standardization
- Need a single canonical label value generation across gateway/routing/runtime.
- Proposal: telemetry lib exposes ModelFamily(model_id) mapping table (kept small).
Owner: Logan + Mina.

2) tier label source
- Tier must be derived from auth/tenant config at the gateway.
- Avoid per-tenant; keep to 4–6 tiers only.
Owner: Kaitlyn + Ethan.

3) “reason” mapping consistency
- Gateway reason should reflect the immediate decision, but also preserve a stable error_code for customer payload.
- We may need both:
  - reason (internal, small enum)
  - error_code (stable external)
Owner: Christine.

4) Cardinality audit
- Before GA, run promtool + TSDB stats in canary:
  - Top 20 time series by cardinality
  - Track series growth over time
Owner: Allison.

5) Sampling / scrape intervals
- Runtime gauges may be noisy; recommend 15s scrape for queue depth and saturation ratio, 30s acceptable for others.
- Histograms can be expensive; ensure we cap bucket count.
Owner: Sofia + Logan.


Appendix: Tuning log (append-only)
- 2025-11-06: Lowered initial paging threshold for overload_ratio from 5% to 2% during canary after observing customer-visible retries at ~3%.
- 2025-11-18: Added gating condition req_rate > 50 to avoid overnight noise in eu-central.
- 2025-11-25: Added retry_after_missing_total metric after SUP-2860 report; set notify-only until hotfix fully rolled out.
